subject.title: fix(coding-agent): scope CODEX_HOME to prevent OAuth collision with OpenClaw

question: Should bundled coding-agent Codex workers intentionally switch existing users to a clean shared worker profile, or must selected non-auth Codex state remain available after upgrade?
rationale: `CODEX_HOME` owns substantially more than credentials, so either outcome is a user-visible compatibility policy that requires owner intent.

options.title: Define selective migration
options.body: Keep isolated authentication but document the supported opt-in migration for required non-auth configuration, skills, plugins, and hooks, then prove fresh and upgrade flows.

options.title: Accept clean-profile reset
options.body: Explicitly approve the clean worker profile as intended upgrade behavior and require a redacted live transcript showing the documented recovery and launch flow.

options.title: Pause the skill change
options.body: Leave the ambient launch guidance unchanged until the repository has an owner-approved Codex worker-profile policy.

recommendation.title: Define selective migration
recommendation.body: Keep isolated authentication but document the supported opt-in migration for required non-auth configuration, skills, plugins, and hooks, then prove fresh and upgrade flows.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest sustained history over the bundled coding-agent skill and its launch policy.
